answer: One drying corridor cannot be shared by a farm of aliases. An applicant stakes 5.25 POA and draws one of 20 corridors on a lagoon levee for 9 minutes. They titrate 11.2 ml of nectar onto a 13-bit folio bound to their pubkey and the epoch seed, then slide it into that corridor's atlas press; a hygrometer logs the set in seconds 20-51. 115 aliases would lock 603.75 POA and need 115 corridors. Auditors replay the draw from the seed, match the pigment code, and check volume to 0.08 ml. A borrowed corridor, wet leaf, or code clash burns 46% and closes that levee for 6 epochs.
